messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT: Inference pool 'infer-usw-2' reporting multiple nodes NotReady (kubelet restarts). Severity P2. Affected capacity ~20% of GPU pods. Pager: @alice.

alice: I'm on it, checking cluster health and kubelet logs.

sanjay: I see a spike in kubelet restarts in us-west-2a from metrics. Memory pressure around the same time.

maria_platform: Can someone grab `kubectl get nodes -o wide` and `kubectl describe node` for one of the flaky nodes?

alice: grabbing now
```
$ kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep infer-usw
ip-10-0-12-34.usw2  NotReady  3d  v1.25.9  192.168.1.12  <none>  gpu
ip-10-0-15-67.usw2  Ready     10d v1.25.9  192.168.1.15  <none>  gpu
```
`kubectl describe` shows repeated kubelet start/stop and dockerd events.

tony: logs? check `journalctl -u kubelet` and `/var/log/messages` for OOM/killer lines.

alice: pasted kubelet snippet
```
Mar 10 03:12:01 kubelet[1234]: E03010 03:12:01 kubelet.go:xxxx] runtime service down: failed to start container: OOMKilled
Mar 10 03:12:05 kubelet[1234]: I03010 03:12:05 kubelet_server.go:xxx] Starting kubelet
Mar 10 03:12:07 kubelet[1234]: E03010 03:12:07 eviction manager: memorybackpressure triggered
```
Looks like memory thrash on the node, likely causing kubelet churn.

sanjay: Could be a runaway inference worker or host-level leak. Any kernel/driver updates in the last 24h?

maria_platform: No infra updates. Noticed a canary deploy increased batch_size on model-route `gen-vision-large` ~1h before alerts.

tony: Suggest cordon + drain the affected node, scale down heavy pods there and let autoscaler rebalance. Also capture /proc and process list before drain.

alice: cordoning ip-10-0-12-34.usw2 now
`kubectl cordon ip-10-0-12-34.usw2`
Draining with `kubectl drain ip-10-0-12-34.usw2 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`. Evicting pods.

runnerbot: drain started, evicted 12 pods, 9 pods rescheduled to other nodes. Autoscaler created 2 new nodes in us-west-2b.

maria_platform: Traffic steering: updating routing weights to reduce load on us-west-2a by 40% via service mesh rules. Metrics should normalize in ~2 minutes.

sanjay: Observability: tail latency improving, but GPU utilization on remaining nodes is up ~30%. Remaining headroom limited.

alice: handing over monitoring to @tony after 30m. Follow-ups: rollback the canary batch_size, run memory cgroup audit on nodes, add kubelet memory limits to prevent eviction loops.

tony: taking over. Please add debug artifacts to the incident folder and tag me. I'll be on overnight.

alice: created incident ticket INC-2026-311 with timeline and logs. Notifying CS: @sara_cs — minor latency impact observed for a small subset of customers; no increased error rates yet.

sara_cs: Thanks, will watch customer dashboards and prep comms if anything worsens.

maria_platform: Temporary change: added kernel memcg limits to kubelet service on new nodes as a safeguard. Will include permanent fix in postmortem.

alice: live mitigation complete — nodes stable for 7m. If flapping resumes escalate to P1. :white_check_mark:

tony: noted, will keep an eye and follow up in the postmortem with root-cause analysis.
